points.description: Defines DHCP: a network management protocol in IP networks where a DHCP server dynamically assigns an IP address (and other network configuration parameters) to devices/hosts on the network.
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely stated (e.g. 'a protocol for IP addresses') without the server dynamically assigning addresses to hosts.

points.description: States what it is used for: automatically/simplifying configuration of end systems by assigning IP addresses (manual or automatic) and providing additional configuration information such as DNS server, netmask, default router.
points.partial_credit: Half if only a general purpose is given (e.g. 'configures hosts') without naming IP address assignment or at least one extra parameter such as DNS server, netmask or default router.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both a definition (server dynamically assigns IP address and config parameters to hosts) and a use (simplifies end-system configuration, automatic/manual address assignment, extra info like DNS, netmask, default router). Give half for a part that is vague or general. Mentioning replacing RARP/BOOTP is not required; give no marks for wrong descriptions such as DHCP translating names or MAC addresses.
